subject: Run code each time a user launches the app (to update Sys.time() )

messages.author: a72da41186ce5589
messages.subject: Run code each time a user launches the app (to update Sys.time() )
parts:
One of my input values is supposed to default to Sys.time(). It is declared as so:

           textInput("toDatetime", "To:", value = paste(with_tz(Sys.time(), "EST"))),

Unfortunately, I want this value updated each time a user visits the shiny app. Currently, it only gets run once, when the app is run with runApp() in R.

My first question is if shiny server (when I eventually migrate this app to it) will run this each time a user loads the shiny app.

If the answer to the first question is no, how do I make it so this bit of code is rerun each time the app is launched, to give the user the most up-to-date default input value?

I've tried this:

    observe({
    updateTextInput(session, "toDateTime",
                    label = paste("New"),
                    value = paste(with_tz(Sys.time(), "EST"))
    )})

Which I got from the example here:

http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/update-input-demo.html

I've also tried just putting the updateTextInput() code in the shinyServer() function, and putting the updateTextInput() in a reactive. Nothing seems to be working. 

Any suggestions?

Thank you all,

-Mike

messages.subject: Re: Run code each time a user launches the app (to update Sys.time() )
parts:
The observe you did should work, as should having updateTextInput right in the shinyServer function. Maybe the "T" in "toDateTime" is the wrong case?

With newer versions of Shiny, there's an unadvertised feature where you can change this:

shinyUI(fluidPage(...

to this:

shinyUI(function(req) {
  fluidPage(...) # or whatever
})

In other words, rather than passing a UI object into shinyUI, pass a function(req) whose return value is a UI object. Then the function will actually execute every time.

Running on Shiny Server will not, in and of itself, solve this problem; but either of these other solutions should work on both Shiny locally and Shiny Server.
